sentences.text: Janet Fielding is the care assessor from the council.
Janet Fielding spoke to Edith Marsh on the phone prior to this visit.
Pauline Reid is a neighbour of Edith Marsh.
Edith Marsh uses a frame to get about.
Edith Marsh does not go upstairs.
Gary brought Edith's bed down to the front room.
Gary is Edith's son and lives with her.
Gary works at a garage on Station Road.
Gary works from eight to six, sometimes later.
Gary helps Edith with shopping, getting up, and taking her tablets.
Edith can get to the toilet herself most of the time.
Edith uses a commode and wears pads when she is not quick enough.
Gary changes Edith's pad when he is home; otherwise, Edith manages it.
Edith is alone during the day while Gary is at work.
Gary leaves work around half past seven.
Gary sometimes does not return home until after nine o'clock.
Pauline Reid visits Edith most afternoons.
Pauline reports that Edith is left in wet clothes most days, with wet pads and skirts, when she visits at two.
Pauline says Edith is left in wet clothes on four or five days a week.
Pauline says she has helped Edith change when she has been allowed.
Edith receives a sandwich from Gary for lunch.
The fridge has no food in it, only a small amount of milk that has gone off, when Pauline checks.
Pauline reports that the fridge has been empty three or four times in the last few weeks.
Gary puts Edith's tablets out in a box.
The tablet box is on the side of the house.
Edith has not had her tablets for a week.
The tablet box has been full since Tuesday the 17th.
The tablet box contains blood pressure tablets and water tablets.
Edith says she forgets to take her tablets.
Edith says Gary is busy and tired.
